transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Rachel Moore (SummitTrust Head of Platform), David Kim (SummitTrust CISO), Liam Rodriguez (SummitTrust Eng Manager)

Summary:
High-level discovery focused on data residency, logging and retention controls, and options between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Customer is a regulated financial services org with GDPR and US financial compliance constraints; primary concern is where PII/transcripts are stored and what logs leave their VPC. Redwood AE/SE outlined deployment modes, KMS/HSM integration, audit logging, and fallback strategies. Next steps: send security pack, share deployment diagram, schedule deep technical demo.

Topics:
- Data residency requirements (EU/US separation)
- Logging and retention controls for call transcripts and prompts
- HIPAA/HITRUST not primary but want ePHI guardrails for certain flows
- Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for latency/cost and auditability
- KMS integration, HSM support, and key rotation

Transcript:
00:00:00 - Alicia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alicia from Redwood, this is Marcus our SE. Uh, quick roll call?
00:00:08 - Rachel: Hi Alicia, Rachel here, head of platform at SummitTrust.
00:00:11 - David: David Kim, CISO.
00:00:13 - Liam: Liam, engineering.
00:00:15 - Alicia: Great, thanks. We understand compliance and data residency are priority items for you today. We want to walk through where data can live and what controls we offer, and to surface any blockers for Hosted, Dedicated, or Private.
00:00:35 - Marcus: Quick agenda: 1) current stack and constraints, 2) residency and logging requirements, 3) how Redwood maps to those, 4) follow ups and next steps. Sound good?
00:00:45 - Rachel: Yep, that's perfect.
00:00:49 - Liam: Good.
00:00:52 - David: One point up front: we have a strict data residency requirement for EU customers and some US midwest data that must remain in our private tenancy. We also have retention limits on call transcripts and debug logs.
00:01:10 - Alicia: Great, important context. Can you share a bit about the workloads you want to run — are these PII-heavy customer support transcripts or more anonymized data?
00:01:22 - Rachel: Mostly customer support and fraud triage, so yes there will be PII in many prompts. We need both GDPR compliance and financial services controls.
00:01:31 - Marcus: Understood. For PII-heavy workloads we typically recommend Dedicated or Private for customers wanting full control over egress and long-term storage. Hosted can be acceptable if keys and retention policies meet your requirements and data residency regions align.
00:01:46 - Rachel: When you say keys, do you have KMS integrations? We need to use our cloud KMS and not Redwood-managed keys.
00:01:54 - Marcus: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key in some regions — it's an opt-in and has constraints around key lifecycle. We also support HSM for Private deployments.
00:02:10 - David: And audit logs — we need immutable audit trails and exports to our SIEM, plus the ability to exclude full prompt text from logs and only record metadata. Is that possible?
00:02:21 - Marcus: Yep, we expose structured audit logs and have configurable redact rules. You can configure logging to omit or hash prompt/response bodies, and we can stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud-native logging sink. In Private you get full control. In Dedicated we can set up VPC peering and private logging sinks.
00:02:40 - Rachel: What about data flow for Hosted — do transcripts ever leave US/EU regions? We're worried about cross-border copies for backups or monitoring.
00:02:49 - Alicia: Hosted is regionally isolated; we serve requests from the selected region and we have policies to keep backups in-region, though some metadata services and global control plane components may be in separate regions. For strict residency we usually recommend Dedicated or Private. I want to be transparent — there are control-plane elements that are global, but the customer data plane can be pinned.
00:03:12 - David: Control plane leakage is a concern. Can you red-team that — is there any chance customer PII gets logged in global control plane?
00:03:20 - Marcus: Our control plane does not store full prompts. We do have trace IDs and aggregated metrics. We can provide documentation and an architecture diagram showing separation; we can also add contractual clauses in enterprise agreements around not storing full customer data in the control plane.
00:03:36 - Liam: From an infra perspective, network-wise, what does VPC setup look like for Dedicated vs Private? Do we need to open inbound rules for anything?
00:03:46 - Marcus: For Dedicated we typically offer VPC peering or private link; outbound egress to model shards is controlled. You don't need inbound ports to our fleet aside from peering endpoints. For Private (on-prem or VPC) you'll deploy our runtime into your network or a customer-managed cluster, so you control all ingress/egress.
00:04:05 - Rachel: How about logging retention — can we set a per-route retention policy? For example, support transcripts 30 days, fraud logs 365 days?
00:04:15 - Marcus: Yes, per-route retention is supported in Dedicated and Private. In Hosted we have retention tiers, but not always per-route granularity — we can work with enterprise customers to set specific retention rules.
00:04:29 - Alicia: Can I ask about HIPAA? You said ePHI might come up. We do have HIPAA controls for customers who need them, typically via Business Associate Agreement and Private deployments are preferred. Does SummitTrust have HIPAA requirements or is it more financial regs?
00:04:43 - David: Mostly financial regs, but some customers query medical claims in our support flows so we want the option to treat that data as ePHI when it appears. We need the ability to enforce stricter handling on those routes.
00:04:56 - Marcus: We can treat certain routes as ePHI and apply stricter encryption and retention. For example, disable transcript persistence, disable analytics sampling, and route logs directly to your SIEM with immediate purge.
00:05:09 - Rachel: Good. Another question: does Redwood ever use customer data for model tuning or evaluation? We need guarantees that customer data isn't used to fine-tune any shared models.
00:05:20 - Alicia: Short answer: No for Hosted enterprise customers by default; we do not use customer data to train shared models. We can put this in the contract. For Dedicated and Private, you own the model artifacts and we don't train on your data.
00:05:33 - Liam: On performance — if we go Private on-prem, what's the overhead to run the inference runtime? Do you have hardware requirements?
00:05:41 - Marcus: We publish recommended GPU specs; for Llama-like models you'd want A100 equivalent for high throughput, but we also support CPU-only smaller models. We'll share a hardware sizing guide.
00:05:53 - David: About logs again — we want to be able to redact PII before logs leave our network. Is there a way to preprocess or a middleware?
00:06:02 - Marcus: Yes, on Dedicated we can place a proxy in your VPC to perform PII redaction or apply a pre-processing filter in the runtime. In Private you can fully control that pipeline. For Hosted we offer server-side redact as a config but that means text is briefly processed in Redwood runtime before redaction.
00:06:20 - Rachel: Do you support EU data centers and EU-only control planes? We have EU customers that cannot have metadata leave the region per GDPR - it's tight.
00:06:30 - Alicia: We have EU regions and store data in-region for Hosted. For stricter EU-only control plane needs, Dedicated or Private is recommended. We do have customers who run control plane components inside their VPC in the Private model.
00:06:44 - David: OK, what about certifications — SOC2, ISO 27001, and do you have financial services specific controls or attestations?
00:06:51 - Marcus: We are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; we also provide a compliance pack that maps controls to common frameworks. For financial services-specific controls we include architecture diagrams and we can do pen tests and supply pen test reports under NDA.
00:07:05 - Rachel: Can you send that pack?
00:07:07 - Alicia: Absolutely, we'll include SOC2 report, ISO cert, and a summary of HIPAA controls and BAA language.
00:07:13 - Liam: One technical nit — does Redwood maintain KV cache snapshots off-cluster? We want to avoid any sensitive cache being persisted outside our tenant.
00:07:23 - Marcus: KV cache can be pinned to tenant storage in Dedicated/Private; Hosted uses caching layers optimized for throughput but we can configure TTLs and encryption. For PII we recommend no shared persistence and tenant-local cache in Dedicated.
00:07:40 - David: Also we need to know about subpoena/govt requests — what's your policy if authorities request customer data?
00:07:48 - Alicia: We have a policy; we respond to lawful requests and notify customers unless prohibited. For Private/on-prem deployments, you'd control that process; for Dedicated we can include notification clauses in the contract.
00:08:00 - Rachel: Good. Any competitors or gotchas we should be aware of?
00:08:05 - Marcus: Customers sometimes compare our Hosted ease to Anthropic/OpenAI. The tradeoff is control — those vendors may have different residency guarantees. We focus on giving options to move from Hosted to Dedicated to Private with predictable SLAs.
00:08:18 - Liam: What's the timeline for a pilot? We're targeting a POC in Q2, low-risk subset of traffic routed to Redwood in a dedicated tenant.
00:08:26 - Alicia: That sounds doable. Next steps would be: we send the security/compliance pack, Marcus sets up a deep-dive and sizing session with your infra, and we provide pricing for a Dedicated pilot.
00:08:38 - David: Can we get a written statement about not using data for model training?
00:08:41 - Alicia: Yes, we'll include that in the security pack and contract notes.
00:08:45 - Rachel: Perfect.
00:08:47 - Marcus: Quick follow up question — for fraud triage do you need low-latency synchronous generation or is batched async okay?
00:08:55 - Liam: Low-latency sync is preferred for support flows; for offline analytics batch is fine.
00:09:01 - Marcus: For low-latency we recommend Dedicated in-region with prefix caching and KV warm-up. We'll show latencies in the demo.
00:09:12 - Alicia: Alright let's go through some notes for follow ups...
00:09:17 - (cross-talk)
00:09:20 - Alicia: Action items and recap: we'll send the compliance pack and BAA draft, Marcus will share deployment diagrams and schedule the technical deep dive, David will provide the compliance questionnaire. Any other items?
00:09:34 - David: I'll also send an example retention policy doc.
00:09:37 - Rachel: Please include estimated costs for 99th percentile latency SLO and for a Dedicated 8-GPU pilot.
00:09:44 - Alicia: Noted. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and update the CRM.
00:09:49 - Liam: Thanks all.
00:09:50 - Alicia: Meeting end.

Post-meeting notes (auto-generated):
- Customer highly likely to require Dedicated or Private for strict residency and PII handling.
- Hosted may be acceptable for non-PII or limited EU-only customers if contract + region controls suffice.
- Key asks: SOC2/ISO/HIPAA docs, BAA language, deployment diagram, per-route retention controls, KMS integration, and pricing for Dedicated pilot.
- Next call: technical deep-dive to cover VPC peering, proxy redaction, KV cache placement, and hardware sizing.
